correctness.rationale: A direct symbolic four-variable determinant factorization into Vandermonde times h2 was verified. Vandermonde on the first three Fourier rows forces rank at least 3. Prime-power cyclotomic evaluation at 1 restricts h2 zeros to p=2 or p=5. At p=2 a 1+3 parity split is impossible by odd root-count, while 2+2 forces an antipodal pair and exact unit-circle solving yields the fourth- and eighth-root families, with orbit sizes N/4 and N. At p=5 a degree-five relative cyclotomic basis and an exhaustive four-residue pair-sum multiplicity lemma force a single fifth-torsion coset and N four-subsets. The proof applies for all prime-power N>5. Replayed standalone integer cyclotomic reductions independently check 915,793 four-column minors at ten orders, with no contradictions; finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Within the canonical four-row family {0,1,2,d}, the choice d=5 is the first quadratic Schur determinant after the Vandermonde case d=3 and linear case d=4; this makes the selected object structurally motivated rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. A harmonic Fourier frame’s full-spark property says only whether one 4-sample failure exists. The exact number and geometry of unrecoverable four-column samples determine a meaningful erasure-robustness invariant. This complete census at every prime-power dimension gives two genuinely distinct binary translation-orbit obstructions, a five-adic omission family, and an explicit prime dichotomy with closed defect counts, eliminating exponential enumeration. This is not a restatement of full-spark existence or a numerical curiosity.
